name: LevelGauge
description:
A small ordered scale — Low, Moderate, High — showing where something stands: segments
fill to the level in its tone, and the level's name follows in that tone's text colour.
An earlier level (before mitigation) stays visible: segments it reached are traced in its
tone when the level came down, and the segments gained are striped when it rose. With
`onPress` the whole gauge is a button.
signature: <V extends string = string>({ label, levels, value, previous, previousLabel, note, size, onPress, fallback, className, }: LevelGaugeProps<V>): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: fallback
props.description: Shown instead of the level's name when `value` is not on the scale. Default "Not rated".

props.name: label
props.description: What is rated: "Final risk". Part of the accessible name; shown above the segments at `md`.

props.name: levels
props.description: The scale, lowest first: two to about six levels.

props.name: note
props.description: One line under the label at `md`.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Makes the gauge a button (an explanation of the levels, normally).

props.name: previous
props.description: An earlier level, such as before mitigation: segments down from it are traced, or striped up to `value` when it rose.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` (default): segments and the level's name in a line, for table cells and footers. `md`: the label, the note, full-width segments and the scale's names beneath.

props.name: value
props.description: The level now, or null/undefined when not rated (the `fallback` shows, in the same space).
